Hoo boy, they’re selling like hot cakes! By my count, 17 bibles unloaded on these Asbury Pines yokels in two days. Feels almost too easy. Smile politely, lament the forgotten morals in the Good Book, quote a couple verses, mention how their naughty little Jimmy or Jane can be saved with their own bible, and before you know it they’re snatching books out of my bag and stuffing bills into my pockets. 

I never had this luck hawking “magic” soaps, forever-lasting aluminum pans or encyclopedias – actual knowledge, hah. How did I fail to notice: all these bumpkins want is to be told what they already think. Tell ‘em that the world is slipping into sin, offer up the bible fantasies they cling to, and then latch onto that teat and milk it dry. Selling hope, it’s all gravy...

That old Irishman –  Sloan was it? Yeah, Mr. Sloan. The bank owner. He bought a bible for each of his 8 grandkids. He’s a fat old lode just waiting to be mined, I can feel it. A big house, servants, two automobiles, and a real trepidation of the world going to hell. I gotta think up something clever… my best work yet… maybe stay in town for a few weeks…

June 30, 1951
Base of Mt. Ulysses, Asbury Pines
Grid 4,8,11 

Amazing. Loess deposits in the soil and fossilized gourds suggest particular regional fertility and planned seedbeds. Very odd – we anticipated a nomadic hunting and gathering society. Yet, scattered across the site: 

- Obsidian spearheads
- Bone knives (ancient bison, caribou, and sloth bones) 
- Clay beads 
- Grinding stones (ancient food processing)
- Woven reeds (baskets? clothing?)

Clear elements of permanence! Signs of organized agriculture would arguably redefine what we know of neolithic North America. How did these people flourish so rapidly relative to their South American counterparts? What was special about this specific society? Who really were these people?

1951 年 6 月 30 日

阿斯伯里松林镇，尤里西斯山山麓

第 4、8、11 探方

惊人。土壤中的黄土沉积与葫芦化石，暗示当地格外肥沃，且曾规划苗床。非常奇怪——我们原本预期这是个逐猎采集的游居社会。然而，遗址各处散布着：

- 黑曜石矛头
- 骨刀（以古代野牛、驯鹿及树懒的骨头制成）
- 陶珠
- 磨石（古代食物加工工具）
- 编织芦苇（篮子？衣物？）

这分明是定居的迹象！有组织农业的证据，很可能改写我们对新石器时代北美洲的认识。相较于南美洲的族群，这些人为何能如此迅速地繁荣起来？这个社会究竟有何特殊之处？这些人到底是谁？
